materials.name: Neural Networks.txt
materials.content:
--- [Page 1] ---
An input layer receives feature values and passes them forward. A neuron can combine inputs by multiplying each feature by a learned weight and adding a bias.

--- [Page 2] ---
For inputs x1 and x2, weights w1 and w2, and bias b, the weighted sum is z = w1*x1 + w2*x2 + b. Weights and biases are learned parameters. An activation function is applied to z.

--- [Page 3] ---
ReLU is f(z)=max(0,z). For z=-3 it returns 0; for z=4 it returns 4. Sigmoid maps real inputs to values strictly between zero and one.

--- [Page 4] ---
Hierarchical feature detection builds increasingly complex representations across layers. Early layers may respond to simple patterns; later layers combine patterns into more complex features. This is a conceptual description, not a guarantee for every trained network.

materials.name: Database Systems.txt
materials.content:
--- [Page 17] ---
A database transaction is a logical unit of work. ACID means atomicity, consistency, isolation, and durability. Atomicity means all operations commit, or none do. A transfer should not leave only its debit committed.

--- [Page 18] ---
Normalization organizes relational tables to reduce redundant data and avoid update anomalies. First normal form requires each attribute value to be atomic in the chosen relational model; a field should not contain a repeating list.

--- [Page 19] ---
Isolation concerns how concurrent transactions interact. Durability means committed changes persist despite a later system failure, subject to recovery guarantees.

materials.name: Data Structures and Algorithms.txt
materials.content:
--- [Slide 2] ---
A stack follows last-in, first-out (LIFO): the most recently pushed item is the first popped. A queue follows first-in, first-out (FIFO): the earliest enqueued item is the first dequeued.

--- [Slide 5] ---
Binary search requires sorted input. Each comparison discards roughly half the remaining search interval, giving O(log n) time. Linear search can examine every item and takes O(n) time in the worst case.

--- [Slide 8] ---
Depth-first search explores a path as far as possible before backtracking. Breadth-first search explores vertices in layers; with equal edge costs, BFS finds a shortest path by number of edges.

--- [Slide 11] ---
A hash table maps keys to buckets using a hash function. Collisions occur when distinct keys map to the same bucket; chaining stores multiple entries in a bucket, while open addressing searches for another slot.

materials.name: Study Skills.txt
materials.content:
--- [Section 1] ---
Spaced practice revisits material across multiple study sessions with time between sessions rather than doing all practice in one sitting. A revision schedule should fit the student's available time and should not be changed without their agreement.

--- [Section 2] ---
Retrieval practice asks a learner to recall an idea before looking at the answer. Feedback helps compare the response with the material and decide what to review. One quiz result is limited evidence, not a complete measure of ability.

--- [Section 3] ---
A worked example shows steps for solving a problem. After studying it, a learner can try a similar problem with less guidance. Useful mistake feedback identifies a step to reconsider instead of only repeating the final answer.
